Under the protocol, that stated movement less the stated take-on is the filing's figure: 69.016m. The adopted figure comes from the p49 triangle instead (79.213m, which recomputes exactly). The adopted triangle sum (pure underwriting years 2014-2021, p49) covers the 1301 RITC but not the QBE LPT.
(1) RITC of Syndicate 1301's 2020 and prior years of account, effective 1 January 2023. Its gross take-on row is 234,962 (GBP235.0m), added after 'Balance at 1 January 1,186,259', so the opening excludes it. The p49 table carries this business on both diagonals of the 2023 step. Its 2019 and 2020 columns run back to the end of each underwriting year, and of the year's transactions only the 1301 RITC covers those years: the 1492 RITC is 2018 and prior, and the QBE LPT is reported in the 2023 year of account (p52). The 2023 steps for 2014-2021 total only +79.2m, too small to hold a GBP235m take-on, so the reserves did not enter the step.
(2) QBE LPT, GBP319.0m gross, booked inside the prior-year line. It sits in the report year's own 2023 column (363,165 gross; 181,582 net, exactly 50% after the Cavello Bay share), so it is excluded.
(3) 1492 RITC. It converts a 2022 LPT that the opening reserves already held, and the filing states no separate take-on amount for it.
The covered part is the 1301 take-on row, 234.962m. The filing does not split 1301's GBP235.0m between the 2014-2021 columns and the 'Provision in respect of prior years' line (421,573; no development rows), so part of it may sit in that line.
Corroboration from syndicate_2008_2021.pdf (p53, not this filing): at end-2021 its triangle had no 2017-2020 columns. Its 2014-2016 values at the 2021 diagonal are 944,592, 1,030,604 and 575,831, against 1,067,606, 1,199,692 and 767,336 in this table (13-33% higher). The Hiscox LPT's 2021 column moved only from 1,539,763 to 1,606,621. So this table restates its earlier diagonals.

takeon_base.carried: The adopted figure is the p49 gross triangle sum. Note 4 (p28) has a 2020 'Less: portfolio transfer' row in the claims outstanding movement, (1,721) gross with 704 reinsurers' share. It raises gross claims outstanding from (175,648) to (186,512) together with the other rows. It also runs through the technical account: the income statement's gross change in provision for claims (6,379) (p17) = (10,795) + (1,721) + 6,137. The filing never says what business was transferred, from whom, or where it sits in the underwriting-year triangle. So it does not settle whether the triangle carries it on both diagonals, in a step, or not at all. The row also appears in 2019 (2,388), so it is not the Part VII transfer, which took effect on 30 December 2020, is outward to Lloyd's Brussels with a 100% quota share back, and has 'no net impact on the balance sheet' (pp33-34); that transfer is not a take-on. In syndicate_2232_2021.pdf (p30, not this filing) the same row prints 1,721 (2021) and 2,388 (2020) with the opposite sign, so even its direction is unsettled.
